timeline.message:
[ML] use_auto_machine_memory_percent now defaults max_model_memory_limit

If the xpack.ml.use_auto_machine_memory_percent setting is true,
and xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit is not set then
xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit is now considered to be set to
the largest size that could be assigned in the cluster.

This functionality will be crucial for Cloud once the Elasticsearch
startup code is setting the Elasticsearch JVM heap size. Then the
Cloud code will no longer be able to accurately set
xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit, so will not set it at all.
Instead the Cloud code will just set
xpack.ml.use_auto_machine_memory_percent and the ML code will
calculate the appropriate maximum model_memory_limit that should
be permitted.
timeline.author: David Roberts

timeline.body:
If the xpack.ml.use_auto_machine_memory_percent setting is true,
and xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit is not set then
xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit is now considered to be set to
the largest size that could be assigned in the cluster.

This functionality will be crucial for Cloud once the Elasticsearch
startup code is setting the Elasticsearch JVM heap size. Then the
Cloud code will no longer be able to accurately set
xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit, so will not set it at all.
Instead the Cloud code will just set
xpack.ml.use_auto_machine_memory_percent and the ML code will
calculate the appropriate maximum model_memory_limit that should
be permitted.

Closes #80415

Arguably this should be `>bug` rather than `>enhancement`, because the Elasticsearch automatic JVM sizing code cannot work accurately in Cloud without it. However, that isn't being used yet and the change probably fits best in the enhancements section of the release notes.

timeline.body:
I initially thought we should filter these on ones where job allocation is enabled, then I saw we are taking advantage of the side-effect of not setting memory limits on the node unless it has the `ml` role. 

This seems possibly unsafe. It would be nice to filter by role here to be explicit and pass in the list of nodes. 

What do you think?

reply.body:
I don't think it's _that_ unsafe.  The code is basically identical to what we've been using for years, just moved to a different file.

But now that we can be sure to have node roles available for all nodes in 8.0 I agree it's better to add the extra check. I'll change the called method to filter by node role rather than forcing every caller to do it.
Doing this smoked out a few inconsistencies in our existing unit tests.  All the fallout from this is in the third commit.
